rv.q: It’s only in the later scenes that there’s much truly pungent sense of pain or jeopardy – yet the relentless energy and unabashed ripeness of the action are irresistible.
This is indeed a musical whose slickness isn't overt, a very un-West End experience that delivers just what fans will want.

This is indeed 'freely adapted' from the original novel, its lead pair of criminals here surviving the police raids and avoiding imprisonment, then giving each other a huge hug and walking off, literally, into the sunset.
This is a simply glorious Oliver!, and a must for family audiences (even if you’ve got to pick a pocket or two).
Too much feels too loud and over-stated.
You'll be leaving the theatre with a spring in your step
It’ll leave you begging for more
Lipkin’s Fagin is not only the culmination (so far) of a terrific career in musical theatre, he is indisputably and joyously the best reason to buy a ticket.
It is a deft and masterful achievement.
Virtually everything is staged exactly as it is in the film.

cn.t: Matthew Bourne's glorious revival of Lionel Bart's beloved musical delights critics with its stylish production and Simon Lipkin's acclaimed Fagin, though some question whether its darker realism fits the show's joyous escapism.
